question.problem:
Express ${\int }_{1}^{4}3{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x$ as the limit of a left Riemann sum.

*Hint: Write down the missing expression in terms of $i$ and $n.$*

${\int }_{1}^{4}3{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[3($
{{field-1}}
$)^{3}\cdot \frac{3}{n}]$
question.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx,
$$

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{i}=a+iΔx.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{1}^{4}3{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=3{x}^{3},$ the lower bound is $a=1,$ and the upper bound is $b=4.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{4-1}{n}=\frac{3}{n},
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{4}3{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(1+i\cdot \frac{3}{n})\cdot \frac{3}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[3{(\,1+\frac{3i}{n}\,)}^{3}\cdot \frac{3}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$
